newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Dec. 23.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Dec. 23.

text.p: All Mexico's major ports were open Monday as of 1000 local/1600 GMT, the Communications and Transport Ministry said in a daily update.
Salina Cruz in Oaxaca state and Puerto Madero in Chiapas state were closed to smaller boats because of wind speeds up to 40 km per hour.
Gulf of Mexico ports reopened on Saturday, including the country's three main crude shipping ports, after a three-day closure as storms hit the region.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Gulf of Mexico, Caribbean and Pacific Coast.

Light rains along the coasts of southern Sinaloa, Nayarit and Jalisco. Dominant winds from the northeast and north at 10 to 15 knots (19 to 28 km/11 to 17 miles per hour) with waves reaching three to five feet high.
Light cold front headed to the Baja California peninsula expected to dissipate later in the day.
Tropical winds bringing humidity and light rains along the Veracruz state coast. Prevailing winds from the east and northeast at 10 to 15 knots, and waves three to five feet high.
Light rains along coasts of Quintana Roo state, with dominant winds at 10 to 15 knots and waves from four to six feet high.
